Q: Matplotlib boxplot whiskers same width as box A:

Since matplotlib v3.6.0 (see this pull request) it is possible to directly set the width of the whisker caps with the capwidths parameter when calling ax.boxplot(). The parameter works just like the widths parameter for the box widths; simply set both parameters to the same value to get the same width for both the boxes and the whisker caps.

You can find an example with an image on the matplotlib website (you need to scroll down a bit).

Q: Chart.js - data points get smaller after hover A:

I saw a very similar behaviour when using:

myChart.update('active');

Changing this to be just:

myChart.update();

fixed the issue for me.

Q: Skip weekends on stock charts A:

I ran into the same problem and needed to keep a true datetime axis for other artists, so I created a Python package implementing an axis scale that lets Matplotlib skip non-business days and off-hours while keeping datetime coordinates. It also allows you to keep using standard Matplotlib formatters. Here an example using `matplotlib.dates.DateFormatter('%b%y')`

https://github.com/saemeon/busdayaxis

import busdayaxis
busdayaxis.register_scale()  # register once at the start of your script
ax.plot(datetime_values, values)
ax.set_xscale("busday", bushours=(9, 17))  # compress weekends (Mon–Fri default) and off-hours (17:00–09:00)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(matplotlib.dates.MonthLocator())
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(matplotlib.dates.DateFormatter('%b%y'))
